summary: The large notification scenario now runs in a fresh deno eval child with --expose-gc, forces GC before taking the baseline, and returns heapGrowth to the parent test. The existing <32 MiB assertion and >38 MiB stream volume are preserved, so the change isolates the measurement from earlier shard tests without weakening the bound or skipping the test.

evidence: runLargeScenarioInFreshProcess starts a separate deno eval child for the large scenario, so earlier tests in the shard cannot affect its heap baseline.
runScenario calls gc before sampling the baseline, and the child is launched with --v8-flags=--expose-gc for a quiescent measurement.
The heapGrowth assertion remains below 32 MiB while the stream still exceeds 38 MiB, so full buffering would still fail the test.
The test is still registered and executed normally; no skip or quarantine was introduced.
